ORDER Heard on I.A.No.1766/2026, which is an application filed for restoration of the present appeal against the respondents No.1 and 2, which has been dismissed by the Registry on 31/01/2019 for non-compliance of Common Conditional Order dated 17/12/2018.
2. Learned counsel for the Insurance Company has not opposed the prayer.
3. Accordingly, I.A.No.1766/2026 is allowed for the reasons stated therein and appeal is restored against respondents No.1 and 2 also.
4. With the consent of the parties, heard finally.

5. This Miscellaneous Appeal has been preferred under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 against the impugned award dated NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8861 2 MA-553-2017 27/07/2016 passed by III Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Indore (M.P.)
in Claim Case No.286/2015, whereby an amount of Rs.1,10,940/- has been awarded from the date of filing of claim petition i.e. 21/08/2012 to the appellant / injured with interest @ 6% per annum.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 6. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the amount awarded is on lower side.
Income has been taken by the learned Claims Tribunal at Rs.4,500/- per month only.

Since the claimant was working as Driver, therefore, as per the circular issued under the Minimum Wages Act by the Labour Department of State of Madhya Pradesh, his income ought to have been assessed at Rs.5,050/- per month considering him 'Skilled Labourer'.

sentences.text: He further submits that in the head of permanent disability, nothing has been awarded.
In the head of loss of income during the period of treatment, income should be enhanced as per the circular under the Minimum Wages Act.
On the grounds, learned counsel prays for allowing the appeal by enhancing the compensation amount as aforesaid.
7. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / Insurance Company has opposed the prayer on the ground that evidence led before the learned Claims Tribunal has been rightly appreciated.
The amount awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal is just and proper and no enhancement is required.

All the factors have been considered by the learned Claims Tribunal while NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8861 3 MA-553-2017 awarding the compensation amount and no fault can be found with in the impugned award.
Hence, prays for dismissal of the appeal being devoid of any substance.

8. Heard and considered the rival submissions raised at bar by learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
9.
It is not in dispute that income should be taken as per the circular issued under the Minimum Wages Act if income is not proved by any cogent evidence.
Learned Claims Tribunal has taken the income of the injured at Rs.4,500/- only, whereas as per the circular under the Minimum Wages Act, income for 'Skilled Labourer' comes to Rs.5,050/- per month.
10. Claimant was 29 years of age at the time of accident, therefore, as per para 59.4 of Pranay Sethi (Supra) , 40% amount is added in the head of Future Prospects.
11. Evidence is available on record that appellant has suffered 12% permanent disability in right lower limp and 10% in the left lower limb and he was operated.
Dr. Kush Bandi (AW-3) has proved the aforesaid permanent disability.
Permanent Disability Certificate is Ex.-P/53.
Learned Claims Tribunal has given findings in this regard in para 14 and 15 of the impugned award.

Even though learned Claims Tribunal has taken into account the injuries suffered by the appellant and also the evidence with regard to permanent disability, but that has not been considered for the purpose of calculating the award amount.
In the considered view of this Court, at least 5% permanent disability in the proportion of whole body should have been taken.
Looking the age of claimant, multiplier of 17 is NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8861 4 MA-553-2017 applied.

12. Accordingly, the just and proper compensation amount comes as under:
Rs.5,050/- + 40% FP x 12 Months Permanent Disability: x Multiplier of 17 =
Rs.14,42,280/-
5% PD comes to Rs.72,114/-
 Medical Bills: Rs.71,940/-

2  Pain and Suffering: Rs.5,000/-

Special Diet: Rs.5,000/-
 Conveyance: Rs.5,000/-
 Attendant Expenses: Rs.5,000/-
 Loss of Wages Rs.15,150/- (for 3 months)
 Total: Rs.1,79,204/-

MACT Awarded: Rs.1,10,940/-
 Enhanced Amount: Rs.68,264/-
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.1,79,204/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.1,10,940/-.
Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to an enhanced amount of Rs.68,264/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
13. Resultantly, the appeal filed by the appellants / claimants is allowed to the extent as indicated hereinabove.

Other terms and conditions of the impugned award including rate of interest @ 6%
shall remain intact.
The enhanced amount shall also carry interest at the same rate.
